s1.syndrome_frame: Acute neurological decline with visual disturbances and multifocal brain lesions in a patient with a history of autoimmune disease
salient_findings: Multifocal T2 hyperintense lesions on brain MRI
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showing elevated protein and white blood cells
Diffuse stenosis and beaded pattern of cerebral arteries on angiography
key_facts: 41-year-old woman with a 3-year history of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis
History of skin sclerosis, Raynaud’s phenomenon, and interstitial lung disease
Positive antinuclear antibody titer with a nucleolar pattern
Negative anti-centromere and anti-Scl-70 antibodies
Admitted with fever and headache
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed protein 161.6 mg/dL and white blood cells 459 /mm3
Brain MRI showed T2 hyperintense lesions in multiple lobes
Empirical antibiotics were initiated
Developed visual disturbances and worsening neurological symptoms
Hypertension and sinus bradycardia on physical examination
Neurologic examination revealed drowsiness, neck stiffness, and weakness
Diffuse stenosis and beaded pattern of cerebral arteries on angiography

raw.champion: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System
raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with fever, headache, and worsening neurological symptoms, along with the presence of T2 hyperintense lesions on brain MRI and a beaded pattern of cerebral arteries on angiography, is most consistent with primary angiitis of the central nervous system. The patient's history of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis and positive antinuclear antibody titer may also contribute to the development of vasculitis.

rejected.label: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
rejected.why: The patient's brain MRI showed multifocal T2 hyperintense lesions in multiple lobes, which is not typical for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, which usually involves the spinal cord and optic nerves.

rejected.label: Cerebral Vasculitis
rejected.why: While cerebral vasculitis is a possible diagnosis, primary angiitis of the central nervous system is a more specific diagnosis that better explains the patient's symptoms and imaging findings.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient's negative anti-centromere and anti-Scl-70 antibodies, as well as the lack of other typical lupus symptoms, make systemic lupus erythematosus less likely.

rejected.label: Susac's Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's brain MRI and angiography findings are not typical for Susac's syndrome, which usually involves small infarcts in the corpus callosum and retina.
